A Field Guide to Software Bugs

content: Bugs of number, and of time, which is number with opinions. Members of this order are small, exact, and wrong by very little. They are the first bugs most collectors meet and the last they stop meeting.

The Integer Overflow
Numerus revolutus
Grows steadily to the greatest size its container allows. At the next step it is found very small, negative, and on its back.
Counters. Anything that has been counting for longer than its author expected to be employed.
Decide how large the number can become. Then ask what happens the day after.
Kourou, 4 June 1996. A 64-bit number was put into a 16-bit space. The rocket, the first Ariane 5, lasted under forty seconds.
Page number to be put right in the next printing. Ed.
Fig. 1. Adult, natural size. The plate was large enough when it was ordered.
The Buffer Overflow
Excessus marginis
Given room for sixteen, it brings seventeen, and puts the last one next door.
C, and everything built on C, which is everything.
Return addresses. Passwords. The caption of the neighbouring plate.
Do not ask a guest how many it is bringing. Count them at the door.
2 November 1988. The Morris worm got into Unix machines through a program that read its input without counting.
